advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the fallback trigger (3rd read) with the prompt's 'commit on the next response' contract so a model met=true verdict is not preempted by an auto met=false.
evidence: Wrapper: 'current_evidence_steps.add(step); evidence_count = len(current_evidence_steps)' then after the awaited call 'if target_id is not None and evidence_count >= policy.max_evidence_responses:' records fallback — this fires on the 3rd read itself.
Prompt (completion_banking.py and completion_verifier.md): 'Commit boundary: at count 3, the next response is commit.' implies the MODEL commits on its next response, not the wrapper on the 3rd read.
The guard 'if target_id not in set(policy.banked_ids())' cannot prevent the override because the model has no opportunity to bank on the same response as the 3rd evidence call.
Confirmed by test test_third_unique_evidence_response_banks_bounded_fallback_before_return: the third list_directory response already returns the met=false BOUNDED_FALLBACK_NOTICE.
'if step in acted_steps: return COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE; acted_steps.add(step)' claims the slot for the FIRST governed call regardless of whether it is an evidence no-op or a real record.
'if is_evidence: if first is None: return ALL_CRITERIA_BANKED_NOTICE' returns after having already added step to acted_steps.
The docstring states revisions are still allowed ('Banked verdicts are PROVISIONAL and REVISABLE'), but a same-batch evidence-then-record ordering blocks the record.
advisory.finding: The bounded fallback records met=false on the SAME response as the third evidence read rather than on the model's next (commit) response, contradicting the prompt contract 'at count 3, the next response is commit' and preempting a met=true verdict the model would issue on its next turn.
merged_from: When all criteria are already banked, an evidence call claims the per-step action slot (acted_steps.add(step)) and returns ALL_CRITERIA_BANKED_NOTICE; a legitimate record_criterion_verdict revision issued in the same model response can then be blocked with COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE and silently dropped, order-dependent.
scenarios: A criterion whose supporting evidence is only fully assembled on the 3rd read: the model would record met=true next turn, but the wrapper has already banked met=false and the id is now banked, so ADVANCE moves on and the true verdict is never captured.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the exact-phrase prompt greps in test_system_prompts_define_the_finite_per_criterion_bank_loop with an assertion on observable behavior (or a minimal set of stable structural anchors the successor code branches on), so benign rewording does not break the test.
evidence: assert "exactly one current unbanked criterion" in compact
assert "use applicable prefetched evidence first" in compact
assert "at count 3, the next response is commit" in compact

The grepped tokens are prose consumed by an LLM prompt; a semantics-preserving reword breaks the test (refactoring-violation criterion (a)) and it verifies wording, not observable behavior (regression-blindness criterion (d)).
advisory.finding: test_system_prompts_define_the_finite_per_criterion_bank_loop asserts ~10 exact English phrases grepped out of the completion_verifier.md reviewer prompt and the successor system prompt. These artifacts are consumed by the LLM, not by a parser/validator/registry; per the Rule-5 litmus an LLM is not a non-human consumer, so grepping prose wording that merely guards the author's phrasing is a change-detector. Any behavior-preserving reword of the prompt (e.g. 'exactly one current unbanked criterion' -> 'a single current unbanked criterion') breaks the test with no change in model behavior, and the test cannot detect a genuine behavioral regression in the loop (that is left to the external eval).
scenarios: A future edit rephrases the prompt state machine while preserving meaning; the unit suite fails though model behavior is unchanged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a completion_tool_policy test where banked_ids() gains target_id during the awaited third evidence call and assert fallback_record is NOT invoked and the result carries no BOUNDED_FALLBACK_NOTICE.
evidence: Source: 'if target_id not in set(policy.banked_ids()): policy.fallback_record(target_id, BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE)'
Source comment: 'A concurrently completed model record remains authoritative. Only the still-unbanked id receives the immediate bounded-search fallback.'

test_third_unique_evidence_response_banks_bounded_fallback_before_return only asserts the fallback DID fire ('recorded met=false' in result; fallbacks[0][0] == 'c00-a'); no test asserts the fallback is SUPPRESSED when target_id is banked mid-await.
advisory.finding: The concurrently-authoritative-record branch of the bounded fallback is not exercised by any test. In wrap_completion_evidence_policy, after the third evidence call returns, the code re-checks 'if target_id not in set(policy.banked_ids())' and SKIPS the fallback when the id was banked during the await (a real concurrency path the comment calls out). Unit tests only cover the branch where the id is still unbanked (fallback fires); no test drives banked_ids() to include target_id between claim and post-await check, so the 'concurrently completed model record remains authoritative' contract has no regression coverage.
scenarios: A model record for the current id lands during the awaited third evidence call; the fallback must NOT overwrite it — this suppression is untested and a regression would silently double-record met=false over an authoritative verdict.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use a _FakeToolset whose call_tool adds target_id to the live banked set before returning on the third response, then assert fallbacks == [] and BOUNDED_FALLBACK_NOTICE not in result.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the completion/memo layering via a behavior-stable signal (e.g. isinstance on the exported wrapper type or which tool the layer intercepts) rather than private class-name strings.
evidence: assert type(completion).__name__ == "_CompletionEvidenceToolset"
assert type(memo).__name__ == "_MemoNudgeToolset"

Both classes are private (leading underscore); renaming them is a behavior-preserving refactor that would break these assertions though the steering->memo->completion->runaway order is unchanged (refactoring-violation criterion (a)).
advisory.finding: test_completion_metadata_adds_policy_between_memo_and_runaway and test_unflagged_and_lookalike_metadata_preserve_the_old_wrapper_identity assert internal wrapper class-name strings (type(...).__name__ == '_CompletionEvidenceToolset' / '_MemoNudgeToolset'). While the composition ORDER is a genuine behavioral contract, keying the assertion on private class names makes it break on a behavior-preserving rename of the (leading-underscore, clearly private) wrapper classes.
scenarios: A refactor renames _CompletionEvidenceToolset; the ordering behavior is identical but the seam tests fail.
